newsitem.title: USA: Cenbank transparency aids frx stability - McDonough.
newsitem.headline: Cenbank transparency aids frx stability - McDonough.

text.p: Federal Reserve Bank of New York President William McDonough said on Friday that economic fundamentals and central banks' transparency contributed to stable foreign exchange markets in 1996-1997.

"Even with the spike in volatility we've seen in recent weeks, there is no question that we have witnessed a remarkable period of relative stability in foreign exchange rates over the past six quarters or so," McDonough told the 39th congress of the Association Cambiste Internationale in Toronto.
The speech was made available in New York.

"Economic fundamentals are certainly one factor," McDonough said. He also tied foreign exchange stability and "continuously greater transparency" or "equal and simultaneous access to the inputs necessary to price assets and their associated risk accurately."

McDonough listed four areas where transparency matters to financial markets -- policy, information, pricing, risk management -- and said "the increased transparency of central bank policy, which is a product of deliberate steps taken by policymakers, is an important aspect of the move toward more transparent overall market conditions."
As an example of central bank openness, McDonough cited the Fed's 1994 decision to announce the outcome of its Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) policy meetings.

"By making information on monetary policy decisions available quickly and broadly, we at the Federal Reserve have helped level the playing field and contributed to smoothing the process by which new information on FOMC policy is incorporated more quickly and efficiently in asset prices," McDonough said.
Turning to financial markets technology, McDonough noted "information is cheaper and easier than ever before."
McDonough noted the faster, more equitable access to information allows financial markets to adjust assets prices "more quickly and more smoothly than ever before."

Turning to risk management, McDonough said "the Federal Reserve Bank of New York has also been deeply involved in efforts to reduce foreign exchange settlement risks," and "been working actively in this area with other central banks."

McDonough concluded that "the evolution toward more transparent foreign exchange market that we have observed in the past several years is largely a product of both technological progress in the private sector and conscious policy decisions in the public sector."
